title: Cognition-certainty measured by evidence — word-of-God less clear than principles
source_text: XXXV. Adde quod, ut ante dictum est, certitudinis illius, quae cognitionis dicitur, mensura, est evidentia. Nam quod dubitationem ex animo excludit est veritatis perceptio, & mentis convictio. Ac proinde quo quis clarius veritatem percipit, hoc ipso a mente ejus longius removetur omnis dubitatio. Non verentur autem Theologi fateri mentem nostram minus clare percipere hoc esse Dei verbum atque testimonium, quam percipit res per se notas, aut conclusiones Logice demonstratas. Non est ergo quod timeant agnoscere assensum illum eatenus esse minus certum.
pass_a_gloss: Add that, as was said before, the measure of that certainty which is called of cognition is evidence. For what excludes doubt from the mind is the perception of truth and the conviction of the mind. And therefore the more clearly anyone perceives the truth, by that itself every doubt is removed farther from his mind. But the Theologians do not fear to confess that our mind less clearly perceives that this is God’s word and testimony than it perceives things known through themselves, or conclusions logically demonstrated. There is therefore no reason they should fear to acknowledge that that assent is to that extent less certain.
pass_b_english: Theologians grant: ‘this is God’s word’ less clear than per se nota / logical conclusions — assent less certain that far.
